text: The Aldermoor hoard, a scatter of Bronze Age ornaments and worked silver unearthed in the chalk fields above Fenmere in 2019, is now on display at the Wexcombe Museum, following a private transfer completed in late September. Curator Elin Voss said the acquisition closes a five-year effort to keep the find in public hands after the objects were conserved at the Northfold Antiquities Lab. The hoard, believed to have been buried around 900 BCE, includes seven spiral arm rings, a broken torque and 31 coin-sized ingots whose use remains debated. Wexcombe officials said the gallery opening, scheduled for winter, will pair the collection with maps of the old ridgeway trade routes that once crossed the district.
